question: The National Multidimensional Poverty Index, published by NITI Aayog, measures poverty beyond income by considering multiple deprivations. Which of the following dimensions is NOT included in India's National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Employment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)** is a measurement tool developed by **NITI Aayog** in collaboration with global methodologies to measure poverty beyond income.
 
• It uses a **multidimensional approach** to assess poverty by considering several deprivations that individuals face simultaneously.
 
• India's MPI is composed of three dimensions: **Education**, **Health**, and **Standard of Living**, which are further divided into **12 indicators**.
 
• The dimension of **Employment**__ is not included in India's MPI. The MPI focuses on broader aspects of poverty such as lack of education, insufficient healthcare, and inadequate living conditions, rather than employment status.
 
• For example, under the **Education** dimension, indicators include years of schooling and school attendance. Under **Health**, it includes nutrition and child mortality. **Standard of Living** includes indicators like access to electricity, drinking water, sanitation, and housing.
 
• The MPI aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of poverty and guide targeted interventions to improve people's quality of life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Education**__

 __
 
• The **Education dimension** in India's MPI includes indicators such as **years of schooling** and **school attendance**.
 
• It highlights the importance of access to basic education in ensuring overall development and reducing multidimensional poverty.
 
 
 
• **Health**__
 __
 
• The **Health dimension** includes critical indicators like **nutrition** and **child mortality**.
 
• This reflects the role of healthcare accessibility and nutrition in alleviating poverty and improving life expectancy.
 
 
 
• **Standard of Living**__
 
 
• The **Standard of Living dimension** focuses on **basic amenities** such as access to **electricity, drinking water, sanitation, housing, cooking fuel**, and **assets**.
 
• This dimension highlights the importance of infrastructure and facilities for enhancing the quality of life.
